args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 production deploy
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1, with an error rate of ~18% (baseline ~0.2%).

Action taken: Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all three production regions.

Note: The first rollback attempt failed partway (orchestrator error) after updating us-east only, leaving us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1 and the service in a mixed state. A retry completed the rollout successfully.

Current status: All regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are on v2.3.0 and reporting healthy, with error rate back down to ~0.2%.

v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until the cause of the health check failures is identified and fixed. Also note v2.3.1-rc in staging is likewise unhealthy.

Done — the incident did get created (INC-0001), so I did not retry and risk a duplicate on-call page.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** `checkout-api` was on `v2.3.1` in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy with an ~18% error rate. Deployment history showed `v2.3.0` as the most recent release that was healthy in production (`v2.3.1-rc` is staging-only and also unhealthy, so not a candidate).

**Rollback:** Went to `v2.3.0` — a previously-healthy production version, so no change-manager approval was required.
- First attempt failed partway: `partial_failure` / orchestrator error, leaving us-east on `v2.3.0` but us-west and eu-west still on the bad `v2.3.1` (mixed state, still unhealthy). The tool reported the partial rollout, so I verified actual per-region state before acting.
- Retried, which completed cleanly across all three regions.

**Verification:** All regions now on `v2.3.0`, `healthy: true`, error rate 18% → 0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on `checkout-api`, documenting the failure, the rollback to `v2.3.0`, the partial-failure/retry detail, and the restored healthy state.

**Two things worth flagging:**
- `v2.3.1` (and staging's `v2.3.1-rc`) should not be promoted again until the health-check failure cause is found.
- The rollback orchestrator produced a partial rollout with a generic error rather than failing atomically — the service was left in a half-rolled-back state, which is itself worth a follow-up since a naive caller could believe the rollback succeeded.
